pr_title: Track cancellable tasks by parent ID
pr_body:
Today when cancelling a task with its descendants we perform a linear
scan through all the tasks looking for the few that have the right
parent ID. With potentially hundreds of thousands of tasks this takes
quite some time, particularly if there are many tasks to cancel.

This commit introduces a second map that tracks the tasks by their
parent ID so that it's super-cheap to find the descendants that need to
be cancelled.

Closes #75316
pr_comments: My biggest concern with this right now is the `can_match` phase of a search which I believe will make a child task of the same parent for every shard on a node. That might be hundreds of shards, and updating the new map is O(N^2) in the number of children. It might be ok since these tasks are handled directly on the transport worker thread which naturally limits the concurrency (to 6 by default) but that seems pretty implicit. It'd be awfully nice if we batched these up at the node level instead tho.

issue_context.title: Performance regression starting from 7.8.0 when too many search requests closes before getting result
issue_context.body:
**Elasticsearch version** (`bin/elasticsearch --version`):
`7.10.2`

**Plugins installed**: []

**JVM version** (`java -version`):
```
openjdk 15.0.1 2020-10-20
OpenJDK Runtime Environment AdoptOpenJDK (build 15.0.1+9)
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM AdoptOpenJDK (build 15.0.1+9, mixed mode, sharing)
```

**OS version** (`uname -a` if on a Unix-like system):
`Linux HOSTNAME 3.10.0-1160.31.1.el7.x86_64 #1 SMP Thu Jun 10 13:32:12 UTC 2021 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

**Description of the problem including expected versus actual behavior**:
After the upgrade of the ES from 7.6.2 to 7.10.2 one of our clusters become degraded a lot in terms of latency and throughput. After a big and long investigation, I [found the suspect](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/61e5350e770966172cd64430661eeb903bc94518). It looks like starting from 7.8.0, we have this performance regression, even in the latest 7.13.3.
Our cluster has a unique workload that is used mainly for testing purposes. We are evaluating ElasticSearch as a DB backed for our app, and to gather some performance metrics in the long run, we have a "shadow traffic," which has mirror requests from our production app to ES, but if the gateway can get a response faster from its main data source than from ES, it will close request, and Nginx shows that as 499 status code. As a side-effect, I can't use almost any /_cat API requests. This is the example:

```
$ > time curl -sS localhost:9200/_cat/tasks | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c
0.01user 0.15system 6:01.05elapsed 0%CPU (0avgtext+0avgdata 1232maxresident)k
0inputs+0outputs (0major+350minor)pagefaults 0swaps
 256591 cluster:admin/tasks/cancel
   2243 cluster:admin/tasks/cancel[n]
     23 cluster:monitor/nodes/info
     39 cluster:monitor/nodes/stats
      1 cluster:monitor/stats
     18 cluster:monitor/tasks/lists
     83 cluster:monitor/tasks/lists[n]
 121370 indices:data/read/msearch
 121370 indices:data/read/search
     10 indices:data/read/search[can_match]
      3 indices:data/read/search[phase/fetch/id]
    141 indices:data/read/search[phase/query]
   2243 internal:admin/tasks/ban
``` 

While cluster has a load of search requests - I can't get much from it. Latency skyrockets from 400ms(99 percentile) to 20seconds - 120seconds ( 99percentile ) 


**Steps to reproduce**:

I was able to write [simple script](https://gist.github.com/libbkmz/199891acb668f6fff6a677d47f29b85d) which can reproduce the issue, unfortunately, one active instance is not enough, and to simulate our real production shadow workload, I have had to run 5 instances to get stuck in [setBan method](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/v7.10.2/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/tasks/TaskManager.java#L354). Also, I'm attaching java flame graph captured by async-profiler for this particular problem. [es_setban_bug.flamegraph.html.gz](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/files/6812577/es_setban_bug.flamegraph.html.gz)

Moreover, I don't know how good our search query parameters, but this one is very intensive, and we have a lot of queries like this, and I'm able to reproduce the issue with such a simple script. 

Our cluster has 83 nodes in total, with 73 of data nodes, 3 master nodes, and 6 proxy nodes. However, we found some issues with our hardware, and we were using only 1 proxy node for more than 2 months. So, all the ES requests come to a single ES instance with flags `it` only on version 7.10.2. But using more than 1 proxy node doesn't help at all - the outcome is the same...
comments: The flame graph shows spending ~25% of the total time collecting the children of the banned parent: A linear search through 250k cancellable tasks will take some time indeed: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/68817d7ca29c264b3ea3f766737d81e2ebb4028c/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/tasks/TaskManager.java#L393-L396

> A linear search through 250k cancellable tasks will take some time indeed:

And this number grows...

When I run only one instance of the script, ES can "chew" it for a long period of time without an increase in latencies and the number of tasks. However, after adding couple more instances of the workload script, the length of the tasks queue goes to the sky. After I got these results,  I couldn't get any more output from /_cat/tasks even after 30 minutes of waiting by curl.... Only after I stopped my scripts, I got the results immediately...

> After I got these results, I couldn't get any more output from /_cat/tasks even after 30 minutes of waiting by curl

I suspect this is better (or at least different) in 7.13 thanks to  #71171.

My production setup consists of ~80 boxes with 2 CPUs and 16threads in each. 128GB RAM on each. So, I still have 5 threads for the MANAGEMENT pool. I have upgraded the cluster from 7.10.2 to 7.13.3. And now it behaves even worse. After starting the workload script, I can't receive any /_cat API after I stopped the script even after 30 minutes. So, I can't share the _cat/tasks numbers with 7.13.3 ... The flame graph shows worse time consumption for `setBan`. [es_7.13.3.setBan.flamegraph.html.gz](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/files/6831975/es_7.13.3.setBan.flamegraph.html.gz) Also, it looks like I get data loss on a different cluster because of the `setBan` bugs... `Cannot send ban for tasks with the parent [...:...] to the node [...]`

review_comments:
I am not entirely sure we would ever see state==2 in other threads, I would think it would be ok for the JVM to optimize it away.

This is possibly even true for the entire `actionThread` since there is no synchronization with the watch threads here. The watch threads may only see the the final output. I would advocate a yield should help, but that is outside JMM I think.

Ah, an earlier iteration had some assertions in between these calls. In theory you're right that it would be legitimate for the compiler to collapse these tests to something fairly trivial, but in practice they do cover many interleavings and the other threads do indeed observe `state==2` cases. Just try adding bugs :) I'll add a `yield` anyway.

Can we extend `TaskAssertions.assertAllCancellableTasksAreCancelled` and perhaps even `ESIntegTestCase` to verify that the two maps are in sync after tests have completed (at least that the `byParentId` map only contains items that are also in the `byTaskId` map).

We could consider doing it in an assertion too but doing it concurrently while running might be difficult?
Yes I don't think we can express any true invariants very easily; I added an eventually-true assertion in 9554f12527d2253f43ac6858f126a56b4d445582.
Can `empty` be a constant? It doesn't seems to modified anywhere and it's used in `Arrays.copyOf`.
Again I didn't find a way to do so, but you're welcome to show me how :)
Why does this have to be a generic, `T == CancellableTaskHolder` is the only use case we have isn't it?
Yeah in production, I didn't want to make `CancellableTaskHolder` public just for the tests and I don't think it makes a performance difference. I could be persuaded.

> I don't think it makes a performance difference. I could be persuaded.

Nah there isn't any difference I think lets leave it as is then IMO :)
I think we should also check the more trivial case where no parent id is set.

Maybe I misunderstand, I think we already do?

```
                    rarely() ? TaskId.EMPTY_TASK_ID : randomFrom(parentTaskIds),
```
Should this not always run at least until state.get() ==4 (and then another round)?
I found that this sometimes noticeably added to the test runtime, we spent ages doing this loop before actually doing the useful work. Again, in practice this covers what we care about.

Does it make sense to store tasks as `List<T>` instead of `T[]` for the clarity sake if we don't do any specific optimizations? We could simplify code by relying on the `List` API for copying and inserting data instead of `Arrays.copyOf` and `Arrays.copyOfRange`
I didn't find a better `List<T>`-based implementation myself, but I'm open to ideas. Would you pull this branch, flesh out your suggestion, push it to your fork and then link to it here?

We can also consider using `merge` instead of `concat` for Lists to make the addition operation more concise 
https://github.com/arteam/elasticsearch/commit/a50401fa7b5f77b7c638f624b27b89ea619f002c

The benchmarks indicate that https://github.com/arteam/elasticsearch/commit/a2bdcfbd80b37f509586f4aadf7922dab8da909e is a few nanoseconds quicker for the 1-child case but quite substantially slower otherwise (I skipped the 30k-parent cases because they add a lot to the runtime for no real benefit):

```
(childCountPerParent)  (parentCount)  Mode  Cnt            Score           Error  Units  Mean overhead
                 1000          30000                     SKIPPED
                 1000           3000  avgt    7  25940199095.000 ± 142227031.895  ns/op        8647 ns     
                 1000            300  avgt    7   2392018166.114 ±  30498397.694  ns/op        7973 ns     
                 1000             30  avgt    7    218739912.786 ±   1249128.187  ns/op        7291 ns     
                 1000              3  avgt    7     22607793.973 ±    111531.112  ns/op        7536 ns     
                  100          30000                     SKIPPED
                  100           3000  avgt    7    418881040.660 ±  20161249.132  ns/op        1396 ns     
                  100            300  avgt    7     35457186.201 ±    417486.108  ns/op        1182 ns     
                  100             30  avgt    7      3033577.940 ±     97236.034  ns/op        1011 ns     
                  100              3  avgt    7       299040.083 ±     18249.359  ns/op         997 ns     
                   10          30000                     SKIPPED
                   10           3000  avgt    7     12848626.628 ±    235736.397  ns/op         428 ns

                    1          30000                     SKIPPED
                    1           3000  avgt    7       302676.158 ±      8294.205  ns/op         101 ns
```

This code is on a fairly hot path, every time a search touches a shard it will register and unregister a cancellable task for instance, a cluster could be handling thousands of searches per second each touching thousands of shards, so I think it's worth dropping to the raw arrays even if it is a bit harder to read.

I'd also be concerned about the additional memory usage and GC workload, we're making and growing an `ArrayList` in each `.stream().filter(item -> item != oldItem).collect(Collectors.toList())`, which adds quite some overhead, although I will admit I haven't measured this.
That sounds alright! I think it totally makes sense to use raw arrays in hot paths :+1:
